# Dennie Ordynskyi

> Product designer with 14+ years turning complex problems into simple, intelligent products — working at the intersection of product, AI and technology, from early concept to shipped experience. Currently designing large-scale consumer experiences at DraftKings; founder of Numi, Tysha and Karta, three products he designed, built and shipped himself.

## About
- Name: Dennie Ordynskyi (Denys Ordynskyi)
- Role: Product Designer
- Location: Kyiv, Ukraine · works remotely with teams in the US and Europe
- Currently: Product Designer at DraftKings; Founder & Designer of [Numi](https://getnumi.app) and [Tysha](https://tyshaapp.com)
- Focus: AI-powered products, intelligent UX, product strategy and discovery, mobile and web apps, design systems, rapid prototyping, human-AI interaction
- Languages: Ukrainian (native), English (professional), Russian (professional)
- Status: Open to senior / staff / lead product design roles and select collaborations with product companies, AI startups and founders

## Expertise
- 0→1 product design: turning early ideas, messy requirements and technical constraints into clear product direction, flows and polished experiences
- AI & intelligent products: designing around AI, automation and probabilistic systems, where trust, feedback and human control matter as much as the interface
- Complex product UX: simplifying workflows, information-heavy interfaces and multi-step systems without stripping away the power experienced users need
- Design systems & scale: reusable systems that keep products consistent, help teams move faster and let design survive beyond the first release
- Builder, not only a designer: designs, prototypes and ships his own products end-to-end (Numi, Tysha, Karta)

## Ways he can help
- Product direction & discovery; UX & product audits; rapid product prototyping; AI product design; design systems & product foundations; 0→1 product design
- Engagements range from joining a product team to helping a founder get from an idea to something real. See [Ways I can help](https://imdennie.com/#help). No pricing is published.

## Selected work
- [Numi](https://getnumi.app): AI-powered nutrition tracker for iPhone — snap a photo to instantly log calories, macros and micronutrients, with a personalized "Metabolic Fingerprint", plus fasting, weight and hydration tracking. Dennie's own product, designed and built end-to-end.
- [Tysha](https://tyshaapp.com): White-noise iOS app for new parents ("white noise for the 3am shift") — real-time white/pink/brown noise mixing, saveable Rooms, a fading sleep timer, Siri control, fully offline with no ads or accounts. On the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/tysha-baby-sleep-sounds/id6783016339). Dennie's own product, designed and built end-to-end.
- [Karta](https://karta-nu.vercel.app/): QR ordering and payment web platform for restaurants — guests scan one code to browse, order, split and pay in their own language; owners get a real-time floor plan, menu editor, analytics, auto-routed payment splits and an AI "help me choose" waiter. Dennie's own product, designed and built end-to-end.
- [Linc](https://linc.cloud): Cloud studio platform-as-a-service; founding designer who built the design system and end-to-end UX.
- [MyGoTrainer](https://imdennie.com/#track-record): iOS marketplace connecting clients, personal trainers and facilities; owned the full UI/UX.
- [Shipshape](https://imdennie.com/#track-record): Smart-home connected hardware; led product look-and-feel and packaging.
- [Chatbox](https://imdennie.com/#track-record): Customer messaging SaaS; where Dennie started as a product designer.
- [E-commerce work](https://imdennie.com/#track-record): Built retail experiences and design practices, scaling an agency into an e-commerce brand.

## Case studies
- [Numi case study](https://imdennie.com/case/numi.html): How Numi turns food logging into a single photo — problem, product thinking, personas, key UX/UI decisions, design system and outcomes for an AI nutrition app. Currently in beta.
- [Tysha case study](https://imdennie.com/case/tysha.html): Designing a baby-sleep white-noise app for the 3 a.m. shift — one-handed, offline, half-asleep-proof. Live on the App Store (5.0 rating).
- [Karta case study](https://imdennie.com/case/karta.html): One QR code for a whole restaurant — designing a two-sided ordering and payment platform (guest web app + owner back office) end-to-end.

## Writing
- [Blog](https://imdennie.com/blog/): Practical writing on design careers, AI products, and building apps solo
- [How to become a product designer in 2026](https://imdennie.com/blog/how-to-become-a-product-designer.html): Career guide from 14 years in the field
- [Shipping two iOS apps solo with AI](https://imdennie.com/blog/shipping-apps-solo-with-ai.html): What AI changed about a designer's job
- [Designing AI products](https://imdennie.com/blog/designing-ai-products.html): Six UX lessons from building the Numi AI nutrition app
- [AI product design: designing for the cost of being wrong](https://imdennie.com/blog/ai-product-design.html): AI product design comes down to one variable: your feature can be confidently wrong. Here is the wrongness budget, draft versus commit surfaces, and what shipped.
- [UX for machine learning: the interface is a measuring device](https://imdennie.com/blog/ux-for-machine-learning-the-interface-is-a-measuring-device.html): How UX for machine learning differs from ordinary product design: the interface decides what the model learns, which fields deserve confirmation, and when to render nothing.
